acceptance_criteria.statement: Exactly 11 top-level domain skills route to 59 current complete workflow subskills under their owning workflows/ directories; no workflow subskill is packaged as an independent top-level skill.
The generic MCP and Rust rmcp authoring skills pass validation and share common rules without duplicated procedures.
No unowned temporary routing artifacts remain in the plugin source or target output.
Same-harness session coordination is documented and does not authorize outbound messages by itself.
The plugin is enabled and nine Codex custom-agent TOMLs are valid, installed in the active Codex agent directory, and loadable after a fresh process reload or precisely blocked.
The todo index matches the current ledgers and reports; task_3 remains unchanged and cost-eval-opt remains a separate follow-on.

constraints: Do not edit task_3 canonical files or harness_factory.
Do not send or queue a message to another session without explicit authorization.
Do not inspect credentials or perform Git lifecycle actions.
Use the existing Codex projection adapter rather than adding a competing converter.
Do not run costly behavioral evaluation during cleanup.
non_goals: Completing the cost-eval-opt behavioral evaluation in task_3.
Changing plugin role semantics or GitHub authorization.
Migrating unrelated workspace files or removing unrelated generated caches.
specification.objective: Normalize agentic-core and workspace tracking while preserving 11 domain skills and their complete nested workflow subskills; verify the full Codex installation before resuming the separate cost-eval-opt task.

requirements.statement: Keep 11 domain expertise packages as the only top-level skills. Their complete subdomain procedures remain under workflows/ and are selected through two-stage domain-to-subskill disclosure; workflows are not separate Agent Skill packages.
MCP authoring skills are complementary, validated, and non-duplicative.
Stale generated plugin scratch artifacts are removed only after proving no consumer depends on them.
Same-harness session coordination distinguishes status, authorization, queue acceptance, consumption, reply, and bounded handoff.
The native Codex plugin supplies its supported skills and MCP components, and all nine custom agents are projected and installed under CODEX_HOME/agents using the existing adapter.
Todo indices link accurately to active work, completed reports, blocked inputs, and backlog while task_3 remains untouched.
